title: Content creators drop the ball
tldr: Ring-light-wielding influencers packed into a luxury suite disrupted a US Open match badly enough that the umpire paused play — a vivid case study in creator saturation and the tension between spectacle and authenticity.
angle: When brand-activated creators become the distraction: the limits of experiential influencer marketing and where 'people over polish' curdles into noise.

title: CD sales are booming as physical media continues its resurgence
tldr: RIAA reports CD sales jumped 45.7% in the first half of 2026, a striking counter-trend in how people consume media and value physical ownership.
angle: The physical-media revival as a signal about audience psychology — why tangibility and ownership are becoming a content-strategy differentiator in a streaming-fatigued era.

title: AI Visibility Starts With Trust—and You Can't AI Your Way Out of a Trust Problem
tldr: Gini Dietrich argues AI-visibility tools can't paper over a trust deficit — trust is a supply chain with stations you can't skip. A useful reframe amid the AEO gold rush.
angle: Why the scramble for AI citations is really a corporate-reputation problem, not a tooling one.

title: Why 'AI Productivity Gains' Is the Wrong Pitch for Every Stakeholder Above You
tldr: Pitching AI as productivity gains won't move a CMO, CFO or legal — the piece shows how to reframe the metric per audience to defend headcount and unlock budget.
angle: How to translate AI value into the language each executive stakeholder actually rewards — a data-storytelling play for comms leaders.

title: The B2B buyer journey now starts in AI search
tldr: The Drum argues the B2B buying process increasingly begins inside AI chatbots rather than Google, reshaping where and how content must show up.
angle: What it means for content architecture when discovery moves from search results to AI answers — the new top-of-funnel.

title: What high-citation brands do differently in AI search: The 2026 AEO playbook

why_fresh: concrete AEO playbook with new rules
angle: From backlinks to citations: rebuilding a content-visibility strategy for the answer economy.

title: Air Fake-Hired a CMO for Six Hours and Made Every Other B2B Campaign Look Like a Hostage Video
tldr: A provocative B2B campaign breakdown of Air's stunt hire, arguing most B2B marketing is lifeless by comparison — a sharp case study in attention and craft.

tldr: Statista data shows more than a third of Americans worry about manipulated or fake news — a trust datapoint with direct implications for comms and media strategy.
